title: Kamino: Efficient VM Allocation at Scale with Latency-Driven Cache-Aware Scheduling
problem: Large-scale data centers require efficient VM placement strategies; cache effects and latency-sensitive workloads are often overlooked, leading to suboptimal resource utilization.
motivation: Cache-aware VM scheduling that considers latency-sensitive workloads improves overall system efficiency and performance in large data centers.
method: Kamino places virtual machines across data center servers by considering two often-overlooked factors: cache affinity (when two workloads share frequently-accessed data, keeping them on nearby processors lets the shared data stay in fast cache memory rather than requiring slow repeated trips to main memory) and latency sensitivity (how quickly certain workloads must respond). For each virtual machine, it evaluates whether a particular server placement would preserve cache efficiency through proximity to related machines, and whether that server can meet the workload's latency needs. It then selects placements that reduce both cache misses and response delays.
key_novelty: The core idea is to optimize virtual machine placement by jointly considering cache efficiency and latency sensitivity together, rather than optimizing each independently.
limitations: Complexity of cache modeling; effectiveness depends on workload characteristics and system configuration.
